rationale: Record the outcome of the extended removed-leader receipt: the sixteen earlier comparisons kept their outcomes (A and B scenarios resolved as before, C's witness, bound and post-step-down comparisons resolved), but C's first premise comparison came back unknown and all five new PreVote comparisons came back unknown, each with missing indices pointing at events of the last scenario - a wiring problem in the enlarged prerequisite set, not an observation problem, since the harness's own native run shows the PreVote behaviour as predicted. The measured account is unchanged; the PreVote refinement stays a source reading plus a native observation until a repaired basis is executed.

interpretations.rationale: The measured account stands on receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 as before: the removed leader answers the read immediately with an index below the entry the actual leader had already committed (parsed index 14), the actual leader's own answer covers its commit index, and the exposure ends when the removed leader steps down one heartbeat interval after the new leader is elected (indices 15 and 16). The extended receipt eaec4096389145f5a26353274b77a639 was meant to add the PreVote scenario; it repeats the C-scenario results (parsed index 14 violated for the pre-step-down answer, index 15 holds for the step-down and its one-tick bound, index 16 violated because the later request is not answered) but its new comparisons are not usable: C's first premise comparison and all five PreVote comparisons returned unknown, each with missing indices naming events of the last scenario (for example [17] for C's premise and [18], [18,19], [19,20], [20,21], [21,22] for the PreVote set), which is the pattern of a prerequisite set that spans four scenarios and admits operations whose result observation the comparison cannot pair. The harness itself behaved as the source predicts - with PreVote enabled and CheckQuorum disabled the removed leader answered with read index 2 against the actual leader's committed 4, one heartbeat tick made it a follower at term 2 with no leader, and the next request was not answered - but that is a native run, not a completed comparison, so no claim about the PreVote bound is added here. The next action is to repair the wiring: give the PreVote scenario its own basis (or declare only the aliases each comparison uses) so that its comparisons resolve, then execute again.

knowledge.assertion: IsSingleton is a size-only test over the configuration and never compares the single voter with the local node.
StepLeader answers MsgReadIndex locally whenever IsSingleton holds, using its own commit index and without a round.
A removed leader keeps leading by default while its proposals are refused and its read answers are not.
Lease-based reads force CheckQuorum, and the lease makes voters refuse higher-term vote requests while they still hear the leader.

counterevidence: The C-scenario results in the extended receipt repeat the earlier receipt's measured behaviour (parsed indices 14, 15 and 16), so the extension did not disturb the established witness.
The PreVote comparisons are unknown rather than negative: their missing indices point at unmatched prerequisite events, so the receipt neither confirms nor contradicts the source prediction.
The harness's native run for the PreVote scenario shows the predicted sequence, but a native run is not a receipt and is recorded only as support for the source reading.
limitations: The PreVote refinement remains source-derived with a native observation; its basis does not resolve and must be repaired before it can be measured.
The scenario requires the application to apply a committed change that removes the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false.
The witness is at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipt shows the returned index is below an already-committed entry and that no confirmation message was sent; no state machine was run.
The forwarded route and other tick ratios remain unmeasured.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts are the same harness family, scenario set, fixture and fault model (four-voter group, entry 10 removing voter 4 with persisted commit 10, voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's acknowledgements delayed). Receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 is the three-scenario basis whose comparisons all resolved; receipt eaec4096389145f5a26353274b77a639 is the successor that appends the PreVote scenario and repeats the same A, B and C events, so its indices 12-16 carry the same meaning as the earlier receipt's indices 12-16 and the earlier receipt remains the support for the measured account while the successor's new comparisons are unknown.
